subject: general
question: According to BIS SP 46-2003, which of the following applications is correctly represented by a chain-thin line in engineering drawings?
solution:
The correct answer is __Center lines.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chain-thin line__ is a standard line type used in engineering drawings.
 
• According to BIS SP 46-2003, chain-thin lines are used to represent center lines.
 
• Center lines indicate the axes of symmetry of objects or features in a drawing.
 
• They are typically drawn as alternating long and short dashes.
 
• Other lines, like visible edges and hidden edges, have distinct representations.
 
• Visible edges are shown with thick continuous lines, while hidden edges use dashed lines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Visible Edges:**

 
 
• These are represented by thick continuous lines on engineering drawings.
 
• They indicate the outline of an object visible from a particular view.
 
 
 
• **Dimension Lines:**
 
 
• These are thin continuous lines used to indicate the size of an object.
 
• The dimension value is placed above or in the middle of the line.
 
 
 
• **Hidden Edges:**
 
 
• Hidden edges or features are represented by dashed lines.
 
• These indicate parts of an object not visible in the current view.
